Title: a couple questions on new cards

Messages.Author: Chris Berger
Messages.Body:
Hey, just a few quick questions... (and a shout out to any of the old
boys who might remember me from before. I'll try not to start anymore
arguments like the great 2nd Tradition Debate... and I won't say I
told you so or ask you to compare the new errata with my old
arguments. That just wouldn't be polite. 8) )

1) Free States Rant - are Independent votes considered "titles" or
just "votes"? i.e. does Kephamos have 2 votes or 1 vote during a Free
States Rant referendum? Something tells me that the votes are
considered a non-contestable title, but I've never really considered
those vampires to be "titled vampires", and I don't remember if there
was an earlier ruling on this.

2) Is the Puppetteer (Wraith) considered a wraith for the purposes of
Shroud Mastery? I have to assume that he is, since the parenthetical
epithets seem to have been a means of classifying allies before
putting the ally class into the text box, but the spoiler text has
only "Ally with 1 life...", as opposed to the "Unique wraith with N
life..." that the other FN wraiths have. More generally, are words in
a card's title considered to define a card's class with the same
priority as the actual text box? (and, on a similar note, is there a
"foo" rule in Jyhad, and if so, is the Muddled Vampire Hunter
considered a vampire? 8) )

>i.e. does Kephamos have 2 votes or 1 vote during a Free
>States Rant referendum? Something tells me that the votes are
>considered a non-contestable title,

- a title
- a non-contestable title
- a non-clan linked titled (like Justicars)
- a non-sect linked title (like all the others)

"Wraith with 1 life. 1 strength, 0 bleed."

The card texts on-line now reflect their type.

Independent vampire with votes printed on their cards ("Joe has 5 votes")

> putting the ally class into the text box, but the spoiler text has
> only "Ally with 1 life...", as opposed to the "Unique wraith with N

Card text says he's a "wraith with 1 life.", as shown on the online spoiler
text list.

> More generally, are words in
> a card's title considered to define a card's class with the same
> priority as the actual text box?

No.
Types in parentheses on card titles tend to match the actual types
of the thing in card text (or in the latest rulings), with the peculiar
case of the Bane Mummies excepted.

> (and, on a similar note, is there a
> "foo" rule in Jyhad, and if so, is the Muddled Vampire Hunter
> considered a vampire? 8) )

No.
